newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Late Reserve Bank support helped the South African rand below the 4.70 level on the dollar in a day characterised by slow trade as business slowly picked up after the New Year.

The currency ended the day at 4.6970/7020 on the dollar from 4.6975/7025 late on Friday after hitting an intraday worst level of 4.7190 during the morning session on the back of strong local and offshore demand for the U.S. unit.

Forex traders said the rand started the year on a weaker note but was soon helped by the central bank which stepped in during the morning around the 4.72 mark and again in the afternoon, helping the currency close below 4.70 on the dollar.
A Reserve Bank spokesman could not be reached to confirm central bank support for the currency.
Despite the sturdier trend in the late afternoon, traders said the bias for the week was still towards further weakness.
A test of the lower 4.75 level was possible over the next week or two as a combination of factors weighed on the market.

These were the weak gold price, speculation of an imminent cabinet reshuffle which would include replacing current finance minister Trevor Manuel -- which has been officially denied -- the stronger dollar and bearish sentiment emanating out of London.
"The rand has started the year on the weaker side and a test of 4.75/4.77 is possible over the next week or two," a forex trader said.
Another commented: "Importers are nervous and keen to cover (long dollar) positions after the New Year."
Others agreed that that there was room for further weakness but felt that 4.75 would be toppish.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading off its low of 8.0178 last week at 7.8992/9123 on sterling and at 0.3326/3331 on the mark.
Local bonds tracked the rand in the afternoon to end stronger after consistent foreign buying during the day, bond traders said.
"We saw some genuinely serious buyers during the day and the fact that call rates (on the money market) have eased also bodes well for the market," a dealer said.
Despite an easing in call rates, short-term money market rates were steady at previous closing levels and the daily money market shortage rose to 10.322 billion rand from 10.236 billion rand before.
The benchmark R150 bond was last trading at 16.10 percent from 16.145 percent late on Friday.
The market was awaiting the release of the November producer price index due out at 0900 GMT on Tuesday and December reserves data due out late on Wednesday.
Economists polled by Reuters expect PPI data to show an 8.7 percent year-on-year increase and a 0.7 percent month-on-month rise from 8.3 and 1.3 percent in October.
Reserves are expected decline to 10.85 billion rand after rising to 10.93 billion rand in November from October's rise to 10.28 billion rand.
Money market rates were unchanged, with three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
The money market shortage rose to 10.322 billion rand on Saturday from 10.236 billion rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 33.48 billion rand on Friday from 1.64 billion rand on Thursday, Bond Exchange statistics showed.
Foreigners were net buyers of 13.82 million rand of South African bonds on Friday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
